# DEXPI 2.0 process examples

Two real DEXPI 2.0 **process** models, from independent sources. Every other model in `data/` is a
`PlantModel`, with two exceptions: `data/exports/bpmn2dexpi/process-model-dexpi.xml` is also a
DEXPI 2.0 `ProcessModel`, and is the only real one supplying `Identifier` throughout, so it
exercises the loader's *strict* path as neither file here can. Those three are what the loader's
reading of real process documents, and its 2.0 -> 2.0.1 conversion, are tested against. The other
exception is synthetic: `data/dexpi_2_0_1/synthetic_process.xml` (and `.json`), a small native
DEXPI 2.0.1 process model generated with pyDEXPI's classes, which holds the 2.0.1 constructs none
of the three real files has -- see [`../dexpi_2_0_1/README.md`](../dexpi_2_0_1/README.md).

| Folder | Model | Origin |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`CO2 sequestration plant - Oslo/`](CO2%20sequestration%20plant%20-%20Oslo/) | CO2 handling and injection terminal | Hand-authored in XMLSpy — David Cameron, University of Oslo, CC BY 4.0 |
| [`Tennessee Eastman - Semantum export/`](Tennessee%20Eastman%20-%20Semantum%20export/) | Tennessee Eastman challenge problem | Machine-generated — Semantum *Model Broker for Diagrams* 2.11.0 |

Each folder holds the original **byte-identical to what was contributed**, a `-corrected.xml`
sibling and a `README.md`.

## Loading them

Process models need `strict=False`:

```python
from pydexpi.loaders.public import load_xml_file

model = load_xml_file(".../CO2TerminalExample.xml", strict=False)
```

Both models omit `Identifier` — mandatory on 136 DEXPI 2.0 classes, 144 in 2.0.1 — on 410 of the
523 objects whose class requires it (CO2 terminal, 78 %) and on 158 of 171 (Tennessee Eastman,
92 %); the counts are the same against either class set. At the default strictness a load therefore
builds 146 objects from the CO2 terminal, against 959 with `strict=False` (47 of its 109 process
steps, no port and no stream). Tennessee Eastman it refuses outright: ten of its `Composition`s
have no owner in DEXPI 2.0.1 (see the limitations below), and strict loading does not drop data; a
lenient load builds 843. The files hold 987 and 876 objects. The 28 and 3 that neither setting
builds sit under class or attribute names the model does not have, the
other 30 of Tennessee Eastman are those ten `Composition`s with their 20 values, each reported with
its XML. On the command line the same switch is `--lenient` (`pydexpi info FILE --lenient`), and it
applies to JSON too: a model loaded leniently and saved as JSON still omits `Identifier`, so read it
back with `load_json_file(..., strict=False)`.

## They fail validation, by design

What a lenient load keeps is not DEXPI-compliant, and `validate()` says so: the MANDATORY rule
`pydexpi_mandatory_attribute_has_value` reports each object holding no value for an
attribute its generated class marks required -- each a DEXPI 1..1, though the twelve 1..1
properties typed `Undefined | X` are not marked yet and go unchecked -- one issue per
object listing its empty attributes. With `strict=False` that is 405 objects (447 attributes) of
`CO2TerminalExample.xml`, 416 (459) of its corrected copy and 159 (167) of either Tennessee
Eastman file -- mostly the omitted `identifier` (410 of the corrected CO2 terminal's 459, 158 of
Tennessee Eastman's 167), then the 36 CO2 ports' `connectorReference` the file connects to
nothing, and a few `description`, `label`, `method`, `name`, `target` and `listOfComponents`.
These files are documented here *as* files that fail it: do not correct them to make the rule
pass. A strict load of either CO2 file reports nothing, having dropped those objects; a strict
load of either Tennessee Eastman file is refused outright, as a DEXPI 2.0 document holding what
2.0.1 cannot represent without loss.
`tests/test_validation/test_rules/test_mandatory_attribute_has_value.py` pins the counts.

## Why the originals are kept unmodified

Between them these two files cover what the loader has to handle in real documents: a required
reference cycle, absent mandatory attributes, unknown class names, unknown attribute names,
dangling references, duplicate `xsd:ID`s and inconsistent topology. They are the regression
fixtures for `tests/test_loaders/test_process_model_loading.py`. Correcting them in place would
delete the test cases.

The corrected copies are generated by [`make_corrected.py`](make_corrected.py), which applies only
unambiguous fixes: a misspelling whose intended target provably exists in the same document, or
an id collision nothing references. Re-run it from the repository root after editing an original.

## Reports

- [`ERRATA.md`](ERRATA.md) — the eight errata reported to DEXPI (filed 2026-10-13 as issues #24
  to #31 of its Specification project), each with the issue text as posted and with
  its evidence by file and line at the specification's tag `V2.0.1`, what pyDEXPI does in the
  meantime and a proposed fix.

## Two limitations to know about before using these

- **They are DEXPI 2.0 documents, and pyDEXPI's classes are DEXPI 2.0.1.** pyDEXPI reads them
  through its 2.0 → 2.0.1 conversion (`pydexpi.loaders.compat`): `MoleFractiona` is read as
  `MoleFractions` and `PercentageUnit` as `RatioUnit`, and the model-level `Compositions` and
  `MaterialStateTypes` containers 2.0.1 removed are emptied into the owners that name each object
  -- the CO2 terminal's one `MaterialStateType` into its `MaterialState`, and Tennessee Eastman's
  `Composition1` into its `MaterialStateType`, which goes into its `MaterialState`. Each step is an
  INFO entry. Tennessee Eastman's other ten `Composition`s are referenced by no
  `MaterialStateType`, and 2.0.1 composes a `Composition` only in one: a lenient load drops them,
  each with an ERROR entry carrying its XML, and a strict load refuses the file. The fractions now
  load as `PhysicalQuantityVector`s. Under the DEXPI 2.0 classes the Semantum export's 11
  `Composition`s loaded but lost the vector in each one's `MoleFractiona` `QualifiedValue`: under
  `strict=True` that `QualifiedValue` was dropped, under `strict=False` it was kept without its
  value.
- **`Identifier` is declared 1..1, and most objects in these files omit it.** Hence `strict=False`
  above.
